data.name: Dysfunctional Systems: Orientation
data.detailed_description:
Dysfunctional Systems: Orientation is a kinetic novel and a prequel to Dysfunctional Systems: Learning to Manage Chaos. It uses text, sound, and illustrations to tell a story and expand on the world established in the first game. There is no gameplay, just click to progress!

What is Dysfunctional Systems?


Dysfunctional Systems is a series about Winter Harrison: a student mediator from a utopian Earth. A mediator is someone who travels between worlds, attempting to resolve the conflicts plaguing them. Dysfunctional Systems: Orientation follows Winter's first week at school, as she learns more about her future profession and the baffling nature of otherworlders. It's a great game to play if the first left you wanting to know more about mediators and their homeworld.

Should I play Dysfunctional Systems: Learning to Manage Chaos first?


You probably should. Dysfunctional Systems: Orientation doesn't assume you have any knowledge of the series, but its primary purpose is to expand on the world established in the first game. Therefore, it is more enjoyable if you're already curious about the details of the Dysfunctional Systems universe.

Key Features

  • Over 23,400 words of story and extra codex content!
  • A soundtrack of 11 unique and never before released songs from CombatPlayer!
  • An unlockable gallery of 30+ illustrations and concepts!
  • 7 new characters to meet and all new sprites!

Soundtrack Included


All Steam purchases of Dysfunctional Systems: Orientation include the official soundtrack absolutely free! Enjoy a total of 11 tracks in both MP3 and FLAC. The album is included with the game files. To access, right click the "Dysfunctional Systems" entry in your library, click "properties", then go to the "local files" tab, and click the "browse local files" button. Look for the "soundtrack" folder.

reviews.review:
Hoh boy this one hurts. 
3 years after the kickstarter, 2 years after it turned up dry and had to issue refunds, we have the prequel episode stretch goal at least, dropping out of seemingly nowhere like a Mediator phasing into our reality from another plane. And what has all this hullaballoo resulted in?  
A... An okay, but purposeless prequel. Oops.

The emphasis is really on [i]purposeless[/i] here. The game follows Winter's first week at the school Mediātōrum as she makes new weird friends and goes to classes. There is barely a plot to speak of, and why should there be? This is an act before the inciting incident, a peek behind the curtains before the play comes on. And all I really see is a lot of stalling and scrambling, with the occasional shining bit of improv. 

I do not envy the creators. They've somewhat written themselves into a corner and encountered the classic problem with Utopias: They're fucking boring. Ideologically interesting, yes - which is why the more dry, educational classes makes for some of the more intriguing bits, though again [i]purposeless[/i] as much of their information is inferred from Episode 1's story and dialogue - but Utopias are unable to sustain any conflict more than mild interpersonal relationship problems. This is why Episode 1 was set on an off-world, as the setting allowed for a driving political thriller that kept the stakes sky high. Here? Winter's a bit worried why her roommate is giving the cold shoulder, in a mystery that resolves itself neatly, cleanly, and with a complete anti-climax. I can buy going for more of a slice-of-life tone, but then you have to deliver on all the messy, complicated, and ultimately, well, [i]chaotic[/i] ways that people behave - an anti-thesis to the world presented. The slice-of-life conflict can't by necessity deliver, and there is no internal struggle to speak of within Winter, and so the lack of a driving plot or motivation leaves Winter a fairly unengaged character, and thus us a fairly unengaged audience. She just kinda bumbles through this episode, stumbling into Scene after Scene with the same 5 whacky characters over and over. 

Which leads to an overarching feeling of: [i]Why?[/i] A poorly thought out stretch goal, yes, but what more am I getting out of this other than words to fill a Wiki page with? 
Perhaps just potential: Some of the character shine in spots of sharp writing, the exploration of lofty ideology and philosophy could easily stumble but always maintain logic and even - [i]shockingly[/i] - have some backbone to their presentation, and Winter is just cute as a button. But there is no meaning here, because there was never meant to be one; we see only the shadow cast of a potential Episode 2 or 3.

Dischan has, for me, always been a group filled with great potential. Juniper's Knot and Episode 1 shows it in spades. But potential, just like dear Winter, is nothing if not actualized. And when you start charging for your hobby projects, especially ones that are [i]this short[/i], you'll need to deliver more than just promise.
